lanes.label: Hope and the ruler from Bethlehem
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Micah the Morasthite sees the word of the LORD concerning Samaria and Jerusalem in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah: three cycles of judgment and hope, with the ruler from Bethlehem, what the LORD requires, and pardon for the remnant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Micah as judgment followed by hope in each section?
ev: Notice the three 'Hear' sections (1:2, 3:1, 6:1)
Name two hope passages (4:1-5, 5:2, 7:18-20)

nodes.t: The LORD comes against Samaria and Judah
nodes.d: The LORD comes down from his temple as witness against the people; Samaria will become a heap and its idols be broken, and the wound reaches Judah to the gate of Jerusalem, with a lament naming towns of Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comes against Samaria and Jerusalem in Micah 1?
ev: Say what the LORD says is the transgression of Jacob (1:5)
Describe what happens to Samaria (1:6-7) and how far the wound comes (1:9)

nodes.t: Woe to those who covet; the remnant gathered
nodes.d: Micah pronounces woe on those who plot evil and seize fields and houses, and on those who silence prophets; the chapter ends with the LORD promising to gather the remnant of Israel like sheep with their king before them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the wicked did in Micah 2:1-2 and what the LORD promises in 2:12?
ev: Describe the sins in 2:1-2 and 2:8-9
Describe the promise of 2:12-13

nodes.d: Micah charges Israel's heads with hating good, their prophets with crying peace for pay, and rulers, priests and prophets with judging, teaching and divining for reward while claiming the LORD is among them; Zion will be plowed as a field.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Micah says is wrong with Israel's leaders in chapter 3?
ev: List who is charged and with what (3:1-3, 3:5, 3:9-11)
Read what Micah says he is full of (3:8)
Say what happens to Zion (3:12)

nodes.t: The mountain of the LORD in the last days
nodes.d: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house is exalted, nations come to be taught his ways, swords become plowshares and each sits under his vine and fig tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Micah says will happen in the last days to the mountain of the LORD?
ev: Describe what the nations say and do (4:2-3)
Describe the picture of 4:4

nodes.d: The LORD will gather the lame and outcast as a remnant and reign in Zion; Zion must go to Babylon, where she will be delivered, and the nations gathered against her will be gathered like sheaves for her to thresh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Micah 4:6-13 says about the remnant and Zion's trouble and deliverance?
ev: Say where Zion goes and where she is delivered (4:10)
Explain 4:12 in plain words

nodes.d: A siege strikes the judge of Israel, yet from little Bethlehem Ephratah comes one to be ruler in Israel whose goings forth are from of old; he stands and feeds in the LORD's strength, is the peace against Assyria, and the LORD purges idols and horses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Micah 5:2 promises and what the ruler will do?
ev: Read 5:2 and say where the ruler comes from
Describe what he does in 5:4-5
Describe the purifying in 5:10-14

nodes.t: The LORD's controversy: what he requires
nodes.d: The LORD pleads with his people, recalling Egypt, Moses, Aaron and Miriam and Balaam; asked what offerings please him, Micah answers that he requires justice, mercy and a humble walk, and the LORD condemns false weights and the ways of Omri and Ahab.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state what the LORD requires according to Micah 6:8 and what question it answers?
ev: Retell what the LORD recalls in 6:3-5
Read 6:8 and state its three requirements
Name the sins in 6:10-12 and 6:16

nodes.t: Lament and waiting for the God of salvation
nodes.d: The prophet laments that the upright are gone and trust fails even in the home; he resolves to look to the LORD, bear the LORD's indignation for his sin, and expect to be brought to the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the speaker of Micah 7:7-9 responds to a world of betrayal?
ev: Describe the lament of 7:1-6
Read 7:7-9 and say what the speaker resolves

nodes.t: Who is a God like thee
nodes.d: Micah prays that the LORD feed his flock and show wonders as at the coming out of Egypt; the book ends asking who is a God who pardons iniquity, delights in mercy, casts sins into the sea and keeps his oath to Jacob and Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Micah ends and what it says about the LORD pardoning sin?
ev: Read 7:18-19 and list what the LORD does with sin
Say whose oath is recalled in 7:20

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.d: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem to worship the newborn King of the Jews, and Herod learns from the scribes that Bethlehem is the place; the star leads them to the child and they bring gifts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of the wise men and name their gifts?
ev: Retell why the wise men came and where they found Jesus
Describe Herod’s reaction
